newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH EQUITIES MKT NEEDS ELECTION TONIC - ANALYSTS.
newsitem.headline: CZECH EQUITIES MKT NEEDS ELECTION TONIC - ANALYSTS.

text.p: The Czech equities market, battered and bruised after weeks of sustained losses, badly needs a good result from the centre-right government in this weekend's Senate elections, analysts said on Friday.
The Prague bourse's PX50 index has fallen by 16 percent percent in the last two months with major issues such as CEZ, SPT Telecom , Komercni Banka and Ceska Sporitelna particularly hard hit.
Analysts said the decline has been fuelled mostly by waning confidence in a market plagued by a lack of transparency.

Adding to the problem, the once stable Czech political climate has hit some turbulence after Prime Minster Vaclav Klaus's centre-right government failed to hold its majority at June elections to the lower house of Parliament.

"If the coaliton loses, we all end up in big trouble -- a minority in (the lower house of) parliament and in the senate, this could make it impossible to govern the country," said Jan Sykora of Wood and Company.
"This would have a severe effect on the market, the economy you name it," he added.

In the elections to the lower house, which were conducted on a proportional represention basis, Klaus's Civic Democratic Party (ODS) narrowly emerged as the largest single party ahead of the left of centre Social Democrats (CSSD) headed by Milos Zeman, the Prime Minister's arch rival.

The ruling coalition managed to gain only 99 seats in the 200 seat body, while CSSD has become a strong opposition voice with 61 seats in the lower house and Zeman controlling the influential parliamentary speaker's chair.

This weekend's elections are being conducted on a first- past-the-post basis with the proviso that a second round of voting will be required in the (likely) event that candidates do not secure more than 50 percent of the vote.
In most constituencies the battle will be fought, between ODS and CSSD, by far the two biggest parties, which opinion polls suggest have around a fifth to a quarter of popular support each.
Although the powers of the Senate are limited, mainly to amendment and delay, the elections are widely seen as a vote of confidence in the government.
A good result for Klaus, analysts said could bring back the "feel good" factor in Czech share trading which has been missing for so many months.
"If the elections are positive I see a big rebound. If ODS win it would be viewed by the market as positive," said John Vax, director of Capital Markets at ING Barings.

He added that there was plenty of good news in the economy to bolster confidence such as the dramatic decline in the growth of the money supply in recent months and a predicted upturn in German growth which could boost Czech exports.
He also said there were signs that the government was seriously addressing capital market regulation and that new systems could be in place by next summer.
